extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in comparative anatomy, craniology, anthropology, and paleontology
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical criteria for measuring, comparing, and interpreting human and fossil crania (capacity, proportions, angles, sutures, sinuses), including methodological prescriptions (fixed basal axis, bisection, tabulation) and cautions about variation and incomplete specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cranial capacity (volume) measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the cranial contents (e.g., by millet-seed or water) to estimate brain volume (examples: 'holds about 31 ounces of millet-seed', 'cranium holds rather more than 36 ounces of water... corresponds to 1033.24 cubic centimetres').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use physical filling methods (seeds, water) and report in standardized units (cubic centimetres/ounces). Compare estimated full capacity (including missing parts) when specimen is incomplete ('entire skull could hardly have held less than an additional 12 cubic inches'). Interpret capacity in context — similar capacity to modern groups can temper 'pithecoid' inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supraciliary ridge development
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of development of the supraciliary (brow) ridges, which may give the forehead a retreating appearance and contribute to overall cranial perimeter ('vast development of the supraciliary ridges').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prominence relative to cerebral cavity and compare with reference skulls (e.g., Australian, Borreby, Neanderthal). Excessive supraciliary ridges are taken as an 'ape-like' or 'pithecoid' character but must be weighed with other features like cranial capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occiput flattening and posterior cerebral projection
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape and slope of the occipital region (occipital protuberance position, lambdoidal suture placement) and the degree to which the posterior cerebral lobes project beyond the cerebellum ('posterior lobe of the brain...must have been as much flattened', 'occipital protuberance occupies the extreme posterior end').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine internal landmarks (tentorium, lateral sinuses) and external protuberances; use photographs/casts of interior where possible to determine whether flattening is real or due to shifted muscular insertions. Compare with reference skulls to judge significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cephalic index / length-to-breadth ratio (brachycephalic vs dolichocephalic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative proportions of skull length to breadth expressed as ratios (examples: 'round...length not exceeding...100 to 80' for brachycephalic; 'oblong...100 to not more than 67' for dolichocephalic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate standardized ratios and classify skulls (brachycephalic, dolichocephalic). Use these proportions to situate specimens within known geographic/racial variation but avoid overgeneralizing from single metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prognathism vs orthognathism (facial projection / facial angle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the jaws project forward (prognathous) or are under the fore-part of the brain case (orthognathous). Use facial angle concepts (Camper's 'facial angle') as rough indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure facial angle cautiously: 'any "facial angle"...can be competent...only in a rough and general sort of way' because points used are influenced by multiple circumstances. Prefer multiple measurements and anatomical reference points rather than a single facial-angle value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of basicranial axis as fixed baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the basicranial axis (developmentally relatively fixed base of skull) as the reference line to which all measurements should be referred ('no comparison of crania is worth very much, that is not founded upon the establishment of a relatively fixed base line').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bisect skulls longitudinally and align measurements to the basal axis so roof and sides are comparable across specimens. Treat the basicranial axis as unity for tabulation of angles and dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angular measurements (occipital, olfactory, tentorial, cranio-facial angles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure defined angles relative to the basicranial axis: 'occipital angle', 'olfactory angle', 'tentorial angle', and 'cranio-facial angle' with stated comparative ranges (e.g., mammal examples and human ranges: occipital angle in humans up to 150–160 degrees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measured angles and compare across series (mammalian sequence to humans). Use these angles to quantify the revolution of sides and roof upon the basicranial axis; supply numeric ranges when available and interpret in phylogenetic/comparative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal and transverse arcs, circumferences, and linear measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure arcs and linear dimensions such as longitudinal arc, transverse arc, sagittal suture length, and horizontal circumference (examples: 'longitudinal arc...12 inches; transverse arc...exceeded 10 1/4 inches; horizontal circumference is 23 inches').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record these measures precisely and compare with reference specimens; missing bones may limit exact measurement of some arcs. Use consistency in measurement technique to enable meaningful comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sutural morphology and suture condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Form, length, and straightness of cranial sutures (e.g., 'sagittal suture is remarkably short (4 1/2 inches), and the squamosal suture is very straight').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and measure sutures (length, closure, grooves). Sutural features can indicate developmental differences or species-specific traits; combine sutural evidence with other cranial characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontal sinuses and internal sinus impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence, size, and openings of frontal sinuses and impressions of lateral/longitudinal sinuses on the interior ('wide openings of the frontal sinuses...a probe may be introduced to the depth of an inch', 'two depressions for the lateral sinuses sweeping inwards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine interior surfaces (photographs, casts) for sinus apertures and impressions; these inform about frontal development and posterior cerebral shape. Note that undeveloped frontal sinuses may correlate with robust supraciliary ridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skull wall thickness and bone robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Thickness of cranial walls and robustness of bones, notably in regions like the supraciliary area ('Australian skull is remarkable for its narrowness and for the thickness of its walls, especially in the region of the supraciliary ridge').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure cortical thickness where possible; thick walls may occur with specific regional types and can affect external contour. Consider anthropological context (use, cultural modification) when interpreting thickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vascular grooves, Pacchionian depressions, and other surface features
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and depth of vascular grooves, depressions for Pacchionian glands, foramina transmitting emissary veins, and other surface morphology ('depressions for the Pacchionian glands are deep and numerous; unusually deep vascular groove...which...transmitted a "vena emissaria"').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record these features as they may indicate vascular anatomy, ossification patterns, or pathology; use them as supplementary indicators of internal cranial arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of specimen (especially jaws) as a prerequisite for certain judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that absence of jaws severely hinders assessment of prognathism and 'relations of the fossil skulls to recent Races' ('formation of a safe judgment...is greatly hindered by the absence of the jaws').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag incomplete specimens and restrict conclusions accordingly. Do not overinterpret cranial-only evidence for facial projection traits; explicitly state limitations when jaws are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative superimposition aligned on basal axes
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare skulls by superimposing longitudinal and vertical sections so that basal axes coincide; deviations of contours then show morphological differences ('sectional diagrams...superimposed...so that the basal axes of the skulls coincide').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reduced sectional drawings or digitized profiles aligned on the basicranial axis to visualize differences in contour, posterior projection, and facial arrangement. This method reveals relative shifts of roof/sides/facial axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological standards: bisection, large samples, tabulation, and avoidance of overgeneralization
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribe that skulls be bisected longitudinally, that angles and measurements be determined and tabulated with reference to the basicranial axis for large numbers of skulls, and warn against extrapolating racial norms from single specimens ('until human crania have been largely worked out...it shall be an opprobrium...to possess a single skull which is not bisected longitudinally...angles and measurements...are determined, and tabulated').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require systematic methodology (bisection, standardized angles/measurements, large comparative series, tabulation) to build a reliable craniology. Emphasize intra-population variation: do not assume individual variants indicate racial characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrative assessment across cranial and post-cranial features
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge fossil specimens by the ensemble of features — cranial contours, sutures, capacity, supraciliary ridges, occiput shape — and, where available, post-cranial bones (limb proportions) rather than by single characters ('so large a mass of brain...would alone suggest that the pithecoid tendencies...did not extend deep into the organization...dimensions of the other bones...show that the absolute height and relative proportions of the limbs were quite those of an European').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize cranial and post-cranial evidence; a mix of ape-like cranial traits with otherwise human limb proportions supports cautious interpretation (e.g., 'revert somewhat towards the pithecoid type' rather than intermediate between apes and humans).
